title: Object access and versioning
summary: S3 access settings decide who can read an object. Versioning can retain earlier versions, but it is separate from access control and backup planning.
introduction: S3 access settings decide who can read an object. Versioning can retain earlier versions, but it is separate from access control and backup planning. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: S3 access settings decide who can read an object. Versioning can retain earlier versions, but it is separate from access control and backup planning.

Version A: old heading
Version B: corrected heading

blocks.title: Object access and versioning

blocks.text: Keeping versions can help recover an earlier file. It can also use extra storage.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain why versions should not contain real secrets.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Turning on versioning does not make an object private automatically.
For more detail later, use this [AWS further reading](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/aws-overview/introduction.html).
